docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Hyperbolic Deep Learning in JAX

Hyperbolix is a pure JAX implementation of hyperbolic deep learning, providing manifold operations, neural network layers, and Riemannian optimizers for hyperbolic geometry. Built with Flax NNX and Optax for modern JAX workflows.

Status: Stable, v1.3.0; see the Changelog.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 8 Manifolds: Euclidean, Poincaré Ball, Hyperboloid, Proper Velocity, κ-Stereographic (signed curvature — hyperbolic, flat, and spherical in one manifold), Klein (Beltrami–Klein ball), Half-Space (Poincaré upper half-space), and Product Manifold (mixed-curvature composition)
  • Learnable Curvature: LearnableCurvature module bundles parameter + reparameterization (softplus, log/exp, or signed identity) + optional clamp; works with any nnx.Optimizer
  • Neural Network Layers: 40+ hyperbolic layers including linear, convolutional, regression, attention, normalization, and PV layers
  • Activation Functions: 5 hyperbolic activations (ReLU, Leaky ReLU, Tanh, Swish, GELU)
  • Riemannian Optimizers: RAdam and RSGD with automatic manifold parameter detection
  • Wrapped Normal Distributions: For probabilistic modeling on hyperbolic manifolds
  • Dimensionality Reduction: HoroPCA (Chami et al. 2021), CO-SNE (Guo et al. 2022, hyperbolic t-SNE), and the Fréchet-mean centering primitive
  • Pure JAX/Flax NNX: No PyTorch dependency; operations work on single points, batch with jax.vmap, and support JIT compilation
  • Test Suite: 7,000+ tests (parametrized across dtypes, dimensions, manifolds) checked against independently transcribed NumPy/SciPy oracles

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from hyperbolix.manifolds import Poincare

# Create manifold (float32 by default, float64 for higher precision)
poincare = Poincare()

# Create points on the Poincaré ball
x = jnp.array([0.1, 0.2])
y = jnp.array([0.3, -0.1])
c = 1.0  # Curvature parameter

# Compute distance (single point operation)
distance = poincare.dist(x, y, c)
print(f"Distance: {distance}")

# Batch operations with vmap
x_batch = jax.random.normal(jax.random.PRNGKey(0), (100, 2)) * 0.3
y_batch = jax.random.normal(jax.random.PRNGKey(1), (100, 2)) * 0.3

# Project to manifold and compute pairwise distances
x_proj = jax.vmap(poincare.proj, in_axes=(0, None))(x_batch, c)
y_proj = jax.vmap(poincare.proj, in_axes=(0, None))(y_batch, c)
distances = jax.vmap(poincare.dist, in_axes=(0, 0, None))(x_proj, y_proj, c)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install from source:

git clone https://github.com/timoklein/hyperbolix.git
cd hyperbolix
uv sync  # or pip install -e .

Requirements: Python 3.12+, JAX 0.9+, Flax 0.12+, Optax 0.2.6+

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to Hyperbolix will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

Two new models, Klein and HalfSpace. Far-pair Poincaré and Stereographic operations are now cancellation-free, and the Poincaré and Busemann layers score tangent input in closed form. LearnableCurvature's clamp keeps the gradient that points back inside, and non-finite input now stays non-finite instead of turning into a plausible finite output. The HELM decoder layers (LorentzMLA, LorentzMoE, LorentzEmbedding) are new. Full numbers and mechanisms are in the numerical stability guide.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Klein manifold (hyperbolix.manifolds.Klein), the Beltrami–Klein ball model (Mao et al. 2024; Zhang et al. 2026). It implements the scalar-c Manifold protocol plus gyro_difference, lorentz_factor and einstein_midpoint. dist has one formulation (version_idx is ignored) and is cancellation-free: median float32 relative error 1.19e-05 at scaled radius a = 4, against 4.33e-02 for Eq. 4 of Zhang et al. The chart holds half the Poincaré radius (a = 6.32 float32 / 13.86 float64 at c = 1). Klein.expmap keeps the factor c that the reference _klein_expmap omits; the two agree only at c = 1. See Klein.
  • HalfSpace manifold (hyperbolix.manifolds.HalfSpace), the Poincaré upper half-space model with HTorch's convention: the height x_n > 0 is the last coordinate, origin e_n/√c. It implements the scalar-c Manifold protocol, and its pairwise operations are cancellation-free. They return inf/NaN past √c·d ≈ 88.7 in float32 (709.8 in float64). HTorch's ptransp is not an isometry, and HalfSpace does not reproduce it. See Half-Space.
  • Isometry maps for Klein and HalfSpace (hyperbolix.manifolds.isometry_mappings): klein_to_* / *_to_klein for Poincaré, Hyperboloid and PV, and halfspace_to_* / *_to_halfspace for Poincaré (the Cayley transform), Hyperboloid, Klein and PV. None of them projects its output. A far point mapped into Klein can land between the proj margin and the boundary, so call Klein.proj after mapping far points in. See The Chart Ceiling and Floor.
  • HoroPCA and CoSNE accept ProperVelocity, Klein and HalfSpace input. Each model is mapped by its isometry onto the hyperboloid (HoroPCA) or the Poincaré ball (CO-SNE), and results come back in the input's model. Poincaré and Hyperboloid results are bit-identical through the new routing (88/88 arrays); HoroPCA's centering changed separately (see Fixed).
  • HELM layers (hyperbolix.nn_layers; He et al. 2025, arXiv:2505.24722).
    • LorentzMLA, multi-head latent attention. Keys and values are decompressed from one low-rank latent point per token, a decoupled slice of the queries and keys is rotated by HOPE, and the score is the negative squared Lorentzian distance over a learned temperature tau = exp(log_tau). Causal, segment (segment_ids) and padding (attention_mask) masks; only HELM's q_lora_rank = 0 path. centroid_form="gemm" is the default, as in HELM's code; "variance" is for short sequences or values far from the origin. See the attention score floor.
    • LorentzEmbedding and lorentz_embedding_init, the hyperboloid token embedding: a ManifoldParam table on Hyperboloid (parameterization="manifold", the default, trained with riemannian_adam) or a Euclidean table of spatial coordinates ("spatial"). c_out maps the looked-up points onto another sheet.
    • LorentzMoE, LorentzMoEGate, LorentzSwiGLU, moe_sequence_balance_loss, MoERoutingStats and RoutingBias: the mixture of curvature experts in the form of the paper, not of the released code. Top-k routing; each routed expert is a LorentzSwiGLU on its own sheet, with a LearnableCurvature starting at linspace(0.1, 2.0, E); routed and shared outputs are merged by one Lorentz centroid. Load balancing is DeepSeek-V3's auxiliary-loss-free bias (RoutingBias.update_bias) plus the sequence-wise moe_sequence_balance_loss. expert_curvatures=[1.0] * E, learnable_curvature=False matches the released 120M checkpoint. The experts run densely (E / top_k times the work of a sparse dispatch), which is fine for small E.
  • Opt-in building blocks for HELM-style blocks; defaults are unchanged. hope_rotate_space; HTCLinear(return_space=True) and HRCRMSNorm(space_only=True); positions broadcastable against z.shape[:-1] in hope/HyperbolicRoPE; per-token weights in lorentz_residual/LorentzResidual, plus LorentzResidual(weight_parameterization="identity", scale_parameterization="exp") and a call-time weight= (with "identity" a trainable w_y can go negative, which gives NaN where the combination turns spacelike; see the lorentz_residual entry under Changed); lorentz_midpoint(form="gemm") and HyperbolicFullAttention(centroid_form="gemm"), the single-GEMM centroid (default "variance" unchanged bit for bit).
  • project_residual_weights(model) and LorentzResidual.project_w_y(), projected gradient descent for the identity-mode (HELM) w_y: called after optimizer.update, they set every identity-mode w_y to max(w_y, 0), the domain of LResNet's Lemma 4.1, so a trained w_y cannot turn the combination spacelike (NaN). Softplus-mode and fixed weights are untouched.
  • hyperbolix.utils.math_utils.asinh, exported from hyperbolix.utils: jnp.arcsinh with an overflow-safe derivative. See the asinh/acosh entry under Fixed.
  • hyperbolix.utils.AUTO / Auto, the default of c_min/c_max in LearnableCurvature and LorentzMoE ("resolve from the parameterization"; None still disables a bound). They replace the private _AUTO/_Auto.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking: LearnableCurvature's clamp keeps inward gradients, straight_through_clamp is removed, and the default softplus/log bounds are [init_c / 10, init_c * 10]. The forward value is still c clipped to [c_min, c_max]. On or outside a bound, the backward now passes only a gradient that moves c back inside: projected gradient descent inside the forward pass, with no extra call in the train step. The old clamp pinned c at a bound for the rest of the run once a step crossed it. In float32 this froze LearnableCurvature(init_c=0.1) under the default log from step 0 (since 1.3.0). Bounds are unchanged at init_c=1.0; identity keeps [-10, 10]. Passing straight_through_clamp raises a TypeError, and so do jax.jvp/jax.jacfwd through a clamped instance (custom VJP; reverse mode and jax.hessian work). See Choosing a parameterization.
  • Behavior change: ProperVelocityGyroBatchNorm's batch mean is the Lorentz centroid of the hyperboloid lift, as in HyperboloidGyroBatchNorm, instead of the log-Euclidean mean. The log-Euclidean mean does not commute with the centering, so the output's Fréchet mean missed the bias point: by 0.73 for a batch centered at radius 2 (float64, c = 1), against 8.2e-3 now. Train-mode outputs change for off-origin batches.
  • Behavior change: non-finite input stays non-finite. ProperVelocity.proj is now the identity (it used to apply jnp.nan_to_num), so the PV norm layers keep non-finite rows. HypLinearPV/HypConv2DPV pass a non-finite MLR score through instead of saturating it at the sinh clip. sinh_lift_to_hyperboloid (the end of HypLinearHyperboloidPLFC, HypConv2DHyperboloidILNN and HypLinearHyperboloidBusemann) no longer clips a non-finite score to ±v_max, which gave a finite loss (12.6 to 13.8) with 4096 of 4096 NaN kernel gradients; the loss now goes NaN at the onset minibatch. HypLinearPoincareBusemann likewise no longer clips an inf logit (e.g. a log_scale past float32 exp overflow) to ±v_max; the row is NaN. In float32, uniform_poincare.sample with n = 2 returns inf radii past √c·R ≈ 89.42. Finite rows are unchanged. See Input Overflow.
  • Behavior change: frechet_mean divides the Karcher step by mean_i(a_i·coth a_i), a_i = √c·d(x_i, μ), and step_size is a multiplier on that step. The fixed step overshot once the batch spread past √c·d ≈ 2: over 60 Hyperboloid/PV cells (float64) it left 24 unconverged after 100 iterations, the new step none (worst residual 4.03e-11). The iterates change whenever a point is away from the current mean.
  • Behavior change: the Poincaré HNN++ layers and all four Busemann layers score tangent input in closed form instead of lifting it with expmap_0 onto a stored point. This covers HypRegressionPoincarePP/HypLinearPoincarePP with input_space="tangent", HypConv2DPoincare, and the Poincaré and Hyperboloid Busemann layers with input_space="tangent". At t = √c‖v‖ = 8, the float32 regression-score error drops from 2.04e-1 to 1.47e-6. At small t the float32 kernel gradient of the Hyperboloid Busemann layers grows like 1/t, as on the Poincaré side. The Hyperboloid Busemann layers now require _busemann_tangent. See Tangent Inputs.
  • Behavior change: the FHCNN/FHNN scale and the Busemann layers' alpha use plain exp. A runaway scale parameter now overflows to inf (float32 past ln(FLT_MAX) ≈ 88.72) and the loss goes NaN at that step, instead of saturating at exp(87.8) through capped_exp with an exactly zero gradient. capped_exp stays exported; the layers no longer use it.
  • Behavior change: lorentz_residual normalizes by sqrt(-c<ave, ave>_L), without abs() or the eps floor. Unchanged for w_y >= 0: there -c<ave, ave>_L >= (1 + w_y)^2, and the output is bit-identical (0 of 27040 probe pairs differ). A negative weight (w_y = -1, or LorentzResidual(weight_parameterization="identity") trained below 0) that makes the combination spacelike now gives NaN instead of the finite point the HELM/LResNet reference's .abs() returns. A past-directed combination (w_y < -1) still comes back as a finite upper-sheet point.
  • Breaking: HyperbolicFullAttention stores its temperature as log_tau (τ = exp(log_tau), always positive), starting at Hypformer's τ = √out_features (new init_tau). An optimizer step could drive the old raw scale to 0 or below, and a negative value makes the softmax prefer the farthest keys. Scores are (2/c + 2⟨Q,K⟩_L)/τ. scale and attn_bias are gone, so old checkpoints do not load; init_tau=1.0 gives the old attention at init.
  • Behavior change: HyperbolicLinearAttention divides its kernel ratio by the denominator floored at the smallest normal number, not by den + eps (Hypformer: + 1e-6). A query whose spatial part is ≤ 0 on a head used to get ≈ 0 from that head, and now gets its attention average. At head dim 4 this hit 2 of 4 random seeds, with errors of 0.74 to 0.81. Elsewhere outputs move by about eps/den.
  • Behavior change: the attention layers keep bfloat16/float16 in and out, and run their softmax in float32. HyperbolicFullAttention and HyperbolicSoftmaxAttention compute the softmax (mask fill -1e18) in at least float32, as LorentzMLA does. HyperbolicLinearAttention and HyperbolicSoftmaxAttention no longer return float32 for bfloat16/float16 input. float32 and float64 results are bit for bit unchanged.
  • Poincaré dist slot 2 (VERSION_METRIC_TENSOR) now runs slot 0's function. Both evaluate the same asinh form; slots 0 and 2 are now bitwise equal in value and gradient. See Slot 2.
  • Cost of the Poincaré fixes. On CPU most rewritten operations and layers got faster (slot 0 dist forward+backward 0.292–0.335× the old time). The slowest is ptransp, 1.112–1.117× forward on CPU; on the A100 its forward is not resolved (1.120, 1.199, re-time 0.984) against identical-code runs up to 1.113. These timings predate the Busemann tangent scores, the sampler fallback and the half floors.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• LearnableCurvature(straight_through_clamp=...); passing it raises a TypeError (see the clamp entry under Changed). The private Poincare._dist_metric_tensor is removed as well.
  • HyperbolicFullAttention.attn_bias and HyperbolicLinearAttention.temperature, two parameters without effect, which Hypformer also has. The bias adds one constant to a row of scores, so it cancels in the softmax. The temperature scales φ(Q) and φ(K) alike, so it cancels in the kernel ratio except through the eps floors; its gradient was 5 to 6 orders of magnitude below every other parameter's. The linear layer keeps the old value t = 1, so its outputs at init are unchanged. focus_transform keeps its signature.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Poincaré dist and logmap were wrong for far pairs in float32. They now use asinh(√c‖x − y‖/√(B_x·B_y)) instead of atanh(√c‖(-x) ⊕ y‖), whose argument rounds towards 1. Two points at scaled radius 7.2 on opposite sides (true distance 14.4, c = 1): dist 14.332947 with an exactly zero gradient → 14.400112. ptransp (the gyration, regrouped in s = x + y) and apollonian_dist no longer cancel near the boundary. Values change for every pair, by ≤ 1.3e-13 in float64. Slot 1 (VERSION_MOBIUS) is unchanged and still saturates. See Far pairs.
  • Stereographic dist, logmap and geodesic saturated on far pairs at c > 0 in float32. They now use the same asinh identity as Poincare. At the same far pair (true distance 14.4): dist 12.656 → 14.39999. Values change for every pair at c > 0; at c ≤ 0, logmap and geodesic are bit-identical and dist moves by ≤ 3.1e-7 relative (float32). See Far pairs.
  • Divisor floors zeroed gradients at capped points. Poincaré divisors 1 − c‖x‖² were floored at their value at the proj cap, which the computed value of 11–76 % of capped points falls below. The floor is now half that value, which none of the measured capped points reaches at c ∈ {0.1, 0.3, 1, 2.5} (very small c can reach it; see the guide). Klein's g_x and the isometry maps use the same half floor. Float32 tangent_norm gradient error at capped points: 1.0 → 3.7e-2. Float32 expmap and ⊕ gradients at capped points stay wrong, for other reasons. See Divisor Floors.
  • Float32 overflow collapsed Poincaré rows to the origin with a zero gradient. HypLinearPoincarePP and HypConv2DPoincare collapsed once an HNN++ score reached √c·v ≈ 44 (43.9 at c = 0.1, 45.05 at c = 1); HypLinearPoincareBusemann once O·sinh²(v_max)/c > FLT_MAX. All three now share a lift that rescales each row by a power of two, so a saturated row lands at the ball's edge (√c·‖y‖ 0.99999994 against 0 before). Below the old threshold, values move by a few ulp. Remaining sites: Silent overflow.
  • JAX's asinh/acosh derivatives overflowed. Their JVP rules square the argument, so the float32 derivative is exactly 0.0 for |x| > 1.84e19 although the true value is representable. Every library asinh call site now uses the new math_utils.asinh wrapper (tangent 1/hypot(1, x)), and the acosh wrapper's tangent became 1/(√(x−1)·√(x+1)). The hyperboloid MLR score reached this regime: at bias r = 60 its bias and input gradients were exactly zero. Reported upstream as jax-ml/jax#40634. See asinh and acosh.
  • Hyperboloid-side cancellations. wrapped_normal_hyperboloid.log_prob transports to the origin with a private transport instead of Hyperboloid.ptransp's Cartesian branch. The FHNN linear and conv layers read the output's spatial norm off the height m directly. HoroPCA centers with Hyperboloid.gyro_difference instead of the Lorentz boost matrix: at scaled radius 8, float32 transform error 0.377 → 1.66e-4 nats. Values change whenever center_data=True; boost_ is still fitted, but transform now reads mean_.
  • uniform_poincare.sample put samples outside small balls in float32, and its n ≥ 3 rejection loop could hang. Both directions of the radius map are now evaluated in half-angle form: at √c·R = 1e-3 samples used to land up to 1.5441·R out, and now none does. Where the loop cannot accept a sample, the radius is drawn in closed form. Elsewhere the samples are bitwise unchanged. For the float32 n = 2 change at large radius, see the non-finite entry under Changed.
  • Softplus inits above 20 were not recovered exactly in float64. _inv_softplus returned x instead of x + log1p(−exp(−x)) for x > 20, so LearnableCurvature(init_c=20.5, parameterization="softplus") with param_dtype=jnp.float64 came back 351887 ulp high. The inverse is now exact (0 ulp in both dtypes). LorentzResidual's softplus init_w_y/init_gamma share the fixed inverse.
  • The Busemann layers accepted the other model's manifold. Poincare and Hyperboloid both have busemann and _busemann_tangent, so the method-name check let each into the other model's layers. Such a pair usually failed at the first call with a shape error, but at in_dim = 2 some calls ran without an error. All four Busemann layers now check the class and raise a TypeError at construction. The other models (Klein, HalfSpace, Stereographic, ProperVelocity, Euclidean) were already rejected. See Tangent Inputs.
  • hope and HyperbolicRoPE rounded the positions to bfloat16 on bfloat16/float16 input, so between 512 and 1024 a position was rounded to a multiple of 4. The rotation now runs in promote_types(dtype, float32), as HELM does; float32 and float64 input are unchanged. Worst rotation error of a bfloat16 input at S = 1000: 4.67 → 0.028.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• New sections in the numerical stability guide: the MLR score at a large hyperplane offset (a half-angle rewrite was measured and not adopted, at 1.9–2.5× forward+backward cost on HypRegressionHyperboloid), input overflow, where float32 overflow still collapses silently, the divisor floors and the tangent-input paths. The Poincaré precision table now holds measured float32 errors, and the chart ceiling is stated per curvature (12.65 / 27.73 at c = 1). The hybrid examples pass Euclidean features with input_space="tangent".
  • Corrected docs and docstrings: the gyro_difference/ptransp chart rule (the Cartesian chart applies whenever either endpoint's scaled spatial radius is at most 1e-1, not only at the origin); an accuracy warning on Hyperboloid.minkowski_inner; _assert_v_max_safe, which bounds one entry only (v_max ≲ 45.05); and the tangent-projection residual in _egrad2rgrad/_tangent_proj.
  • The HELM citation named the wrong paper ("Chen et al. 2024, Hyperbolic Embeddings for Learning on Manifolds"); it is He et al. 2025, "HELM: Hyperbolic Large Language Models via Mixture-of-Curvature Experts" (arXiv:2505.24722). The LResNet entry in the layers API index now cites He, Yang & Ying (2025), "Lorentzian Residual Neural Networks" (KDD 2025).
  • riemannian_adam's docstring explains why it has no geoopt-style stabilize option: every step already ends on the manifold, and re-projecting the moment only loses float32 accuracy far from the origin.
  • User guide and API pages checked against the code: broken examples fixed (e.g. nnx.jit train steps), stale advice removed, numerical-stability.md trimmed to user guidance.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • LearnableCurvature's default parameterization is now "log" (was "softplus"). The softplus docstring's attribution to "the van Spengler et al. 2023 Poincare ResNet convention" didn't hold up: that paper's own reported curvature experiments (Sec. 4.2) sweep fixed values c ∈ {1, 0.1, 0.01} and settle on c=0.1, not a learnable softplus-reparameterized curvature — the softplus(raw) mechanism itself is geoopt's Stereographic/PoincareBall convention, which the released Poincare ResNet code happens to default to (learnable=True) since its manifold is built on geoopt. "softplus" remains available and its docstring now cites geoopt with the code-default note. Breaking for call sites relying on the implicit default — pass parameterization="softplus" explicitly to keep the old behavior

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Origin derivatives now follow the on-manifold Cartesian chart instead of value-only polar fallbacks. Hyperboloid.gyro_difference and ptransp use exact Cartesian formulae when either endpoint's scaled spatial radius is at most 1e-1 and keep the stable polar frame otherwise. Hyperboloid.logmap uses the regular Cartesian expression at an exact origin endpoint and the stable polar frame otherwise; ordinary autodiff follows the selected expression. busemann now evaluates a projected-coordinate branch whose constrained first derivative agrees across q = <x_s,v> = 0, restoring the origin gradient -v for a unit direction. lorentz_midpoint now uses the time/velocity variance form below, preserving the derivative of a nonzero-weight origin point in a mixed cloud. The inherited log-map origin defect predates the preceding polar-frame sweep; that sweep repaired large-radius and collinear behavior without covering every origin endpoint derivative. ProperVelocity.logmap, gyro_difference, and ptransp inherit these repairs through their exact hyperboloid lifts. Public signatures, defaults, and version slots are unchanged.
  • Signed Möbius operations now have the literal curvature derivative at c = 0 for nonzero operands. The stable denominator evaluates separate signed factorizations for c > 0 and c <= 0; both match 1 + 2*sign*c*<x,y> + c^2*||x||^2*||y||^2 and its slope at zero. The existing MIN_NORM radial floors leave only their bounded residual when an operand is exactly zero. The preceding abs(c) factorization selected the wrong one-sided denominator slope at zero, so a signed learnable curvature could receive the wrong update on its flat step.
  • Historical scope of the preceding numerics sweep. The large-radius "rest of the Hyperboloid" entry and the _logmap_direction entry below describe the value and collinear-gradient repairs measured before this origin-derivative pass. Their measurements are preserved as historical evidence; they do not claim that every origin endpoint derivative was already correct. The first Fixed entry records the current origin behavior.
  • Historical value repair from the preceding numerics sweep: the rest of the Hyperboloid's two-point and tangent-space primitives cancelled the same way dist/logmap/sqdist/tangent_norm did before this file's earlier fix: expmap (two-point form), ptransp/ptransp_0, tangent_proj, tangent_inner, egrad2rgrad, the gyro addition (the Lorentz boost, feeding HypLinearHyperboloidPLFC's and friends' gyro-bias), and busemann all formed an O(1) result as the difference of two O(e^{2a}) Minkowski terms, a = √c·d the scaled geodesic radius. At that revision each read the radius off the spatial part and subtracted before squaring, via the shared radial_perp_decomposition helper in hyperbolix/utils/math_utils.py. Not bit-identical: forward values are unchanged up to rounding below the cancellation's onset, and gradients differ from step 0 at rounding level. Measured (4-seed medians, float32, logs/2026-09-08_hyperboloid_tangent_primitives/): gyro-addition forward geodesic error 4.181e-04 → 1.366e-05 at a=6, 1.527e-02 → 9.767e-05 at a=8, 6.557e-02 → 6.802e-04 at a=10 (5 of 32 seeds non-finite as-is, 0 fixed); end-to-end riemannian_adam on a ManifoldParam loses both seeds to NaN by a=9 as-is, fixed stays finite through a=16; the transport isometry |ratio-1| goes from non-finite on 1-2 of 4 seeds from a=9 on (max residual 6.6e+14 at a=10) to 1.192e-07 / 1.132e-06 / 7.557e-05 at a=6/8/12; egrad2rgrad relative error 3.816e-05 → 4.616e-08 at a=6, 1.000e+00 (2 of 4 seeds non-finite) → 1.005e-07 at a=14 — it needs no division by a measured quantity at all now, since ⟨x,x⟩_L = -1/c holds exactly on the sheet, so the 1.2.0 claim that the Riemannian gradient is unchanged after egrad2rgrad now holds by construction rather than by cancellation luck; the aligned-branch busemann relative error 1.096e-02 → 1.585e-09 at a=8, 1.878e+00 → 2.274e-06 at a=12 (as-is pins 1 of 4 seeds on the -34.5 MIN_NORM floor at a=10 and 3 of 4 at a=12, with an identically-zero gradient at a=12; fixed pins none at either radius). expmap's landing accuracy is the one cell that is not a clean win: at a=14 the fixed geodesic landing error is worse than as-is, 3.500e-02 vs 2.410e-02 median (1.45x) — see docs/user-guide/numerical-stability.md for the full table.
  • The Poincaré/κ-stereographic Möbius denominator 1 ± 2c⟨x,y⟩ + c²‖x‖²‖y‖², behind dist, logmap, addition, and gyr, no longer forms the cancellation at the ball chart's ceiling. It evaluates separate signed factorizations built from the radial gap and sum, so subtraction happens before squaring and the literal curvature slope is retained at c = 0 for nonzero operands. The measurements in probe_poincare_mobius_ebebd09.out describe the earlier positive-curvature value repair and remain historical evidence; the signed zero-curvature derivative repair is covered separately above.
  • lorentz_midpoint now uses a time/velocity variance for both its large-radius value and its origin-point derivative. With h = sum_m w_m*x_m, t_m = x[m,0], z_m = x[m,1:]/t_m, T = h[0], and z_bar = h[1:]/T, the normalizer is D^2 = T*sum_m w_m*(1/t_m + c*t_m*||z_m-z_bar||^2) = c*(T^2-||h_s||^2). The direct variance avoids the cancelling Lorentz square and divides only by positive time coordinates, so a nonzero-weight origin point retains its derivative in a mixed cloud. Weights must be non-negative. An all-zero weight row still returns the origin as a value convention; no weight derivative is promised there. Historical measurements of the preceding radius/direction variance form remain documented as historical evidence in the numerical-stability guide.
  • ProperVelocity operations now share one direct hyperboloid bridge. expmap and gyro addition use the bridge introduced at 8e77147; gyro_difference and ptransp joined it at 757a910, and ProperVelocityGyroBatchNorm now centers with gyro_difference. A tangent lifts as (<x,v>/X_0, v) at X = (sqrt(1/c+||x||^2), x), and the PV result is the spatial part of the hyperboloid result. The bridge avoids the Poincaré chart and carries the repaired Cartesian origin derivatives into PV.
  • HoroPCA's horo_projection and ProperVelocity's tangent_inner/tangent_norm inherited the same cancellation, through busemann and radial_perp_decomposition respectively. Measured (probe_midpoint_horopca_busemann_pv_9093ea7.out, 4-seed medians, a = √c·d): horo_projection error (K=2 ideal directions, vs the library's own float64 path, table C.ii) 1.413e-01 → 1.086e-04 at a=8, 3.660e+00 → 8.633e-03 at a=12; Busemann-coordinate preservation |dB| 8.170e-02 → 8.836e-05 at a=8. ProperVelocity |⟨v,v⟩-1| on the exactly-unit radial tangent (table C.iv) 6.250e-01 → 2.384e-07 at a=8, 1.536e+03 → 5.192e-05 at a=12.
  • HyperboloidGyroBatchNorm's centering step, (⊖x) ⊕ y with the batch mean close to x, cancelled in the general ambient boost. It now centers with Hyperboloid.gyro_difference(x, y, c) (see ### Added below). That operation uses the Cartesian inverse boost when either endpoint's scaled spatial radius is at most 1e-1 and the stable polar frame otherwise. Historical high-radius value and first-derivative measurements in step2c_gyro_difference_accuracy.out and step2c_gyro_bn_centering.out predate the Cartesian origin repair; they do not describe the current origin derivative rule. This retires Known limit 1 of docs/user-guide/numerical-stability.md.
  • ProperVelocity.dist/.logmap between nearby points at large radius cancelled the same way the ambient hyperboloid two-point primitives did before their own fix, since PV's tangent-space metric routes through the same Minkowski forms. Both now go through the exact lift X = (√(1/c+‖x‖²), x) onto the hyperboloid and its cancellation-free polar-frame dist/logmap. Measured (step2c_pv_accuracy.out, c=0.5, dim 16, radial step of true Riemannian length 0.1, landing point in float64, coordinate-axis direction): old dist 5.988811e-02 / 4.382994e+00 / 1.056287e+01 at a=8/10/12 (true value 0.1), new relative error 9.54e-07 / 8.05e-07 / 4.62e-07 — inside the float32 storage floor of the same pairs, 9.24e-07 / 7.22e-07 / 4.92e-07. This is the favourable direction: on the same probe's PRNGKey(3) direction, the worst new relative error over a ∈ {8,10} is 1.13e-04 at a=10, against that pair's own storage floor of 1.41e-05. The full float32 chain (expmap in float32 too) used to return 3.167524e-01 at a=8 and 4.369660e+00 at a=10 for a true step of 0.1; it now returns 1.000014e-01 and 9.999371e-02. Equivalence (step2c_pv_equivalence.out): float64 new vs old at a≤3 agree to 8.09e-14 max; against an 80-bit reference at a≤6, dist is 7.11e-15 max against old's 3.64e-11, and logmap is 4.39e-14 max relative error / 1.26e-12 max ‖err‖_x; dist(x,x) and logmap(x,x) are exactly 0 in both dtypes with a finite gradient there. Callers that inherit the fix unchanged: utils.helpers.compute_pairwise_distances, decomposition/frechet.py, nn_layers/poincare_batchnorm.py (with a PV manifold), manifolds/product.py. This retires Known limit 4 of docs/user-guide/numerical-stability.md.
  • Historical collinear-gradient repair from the preceding numerics sweep: _logmap_direction, the helper shared by Hyperboloid.logmap, .ptransp, .gyro_difference and, through the exact lift, ProperVelocity.logmap, normalized a vector that is exactly zero on the whole collinear set, leaving an O(1) gradient error there while the forward value stayed correct. It returned (cos φ, sin φ, n̂) with n̂ = safe_normalize(ŷ_s − ⟨x̂_s, ŷ_s⟩·x̂_s); on a pair sharing a ray (ψ = 0 or π, y = x included) that argument is zero up to rounding, so the normalization's derivative is arbitrary, and multiplied by a sin φ that is itself only O(rounding) rather than exactly 0, it left an O(1) error in the gradient. Pre-existing since the polar-frame logmap of 1.1.2 (2026-08-25). At that revision the helper returned (S·cos φ, perp_y) with no 1/S and no 1/‖perp_y‖ anywhere: perp_y = r_y·[(csum²/4)·(ŷ_s − x̂_s) + (chord²/4)·(x̂_s + ŷ_s)], a non-negative combination of two orthogonal vectors that vanishes exactly on both degenerate rays, and each consumer's own prefactor cancels the remaining S (log_x(y) = asinhc(S)·(2/√c)·(S·cos φ)·e_rad + (asinhc(S)/C)·(0, perp_y); similarly for ptransp and gyro_difference — see the docstrings for the exact scales). Measured (step2e_gradients.out, a ≤ 3, old → new): float64 ∇‖log‖²/∇⟨w,log⟩ on collinear/y = x pairs 2.81 → 1.8e-10; the Jacobian of log_x(·) at y = x vs the identity 1.00 → 5.0e-16; ptransp's ∇⟨w, PT v⟩ f32-vs-f64 relative error 3.29 → 4.0e-6; gyro_difference's gradient f32-vs-f64 relative error 5.94 → 9.6e-7; PV ∇‖log‖² on a collinear pair, float32, 4.1e-5 → 2.2e-5 (1.9x better than even the pre-lift ambient PV spelling; float64 unchanged at 3.3e-10 either way). Zero non-finite entries across every geometry and dtype. Forward values are unaffected: float64 new-vs-old equivalence at a ≤ 6 over dims 2/5/64, c ∈ {0.1, 0.5, 1, 3}, 5 geometries, 5 seeds (step2e_equivalence.out) — logmap 4.7e-16, ptransp 5.8e-14, gyro_difference 3.2e-15, PV logmap 1.5e-15 (budget 1e-12); dist/sqdist/_polar_frame are bitwise unchanged; float32 _logmap at a ∈ {9, 12} worst 1.7e-7 against 2.3e-7 old. New test test_hyperboloid_logmap_squared_norm_gradient_is_exact_on_the_collinear_set measures 3.8e-15 (float64) / 1.4e-6 (float32) against bounds 2e-14 / 6e-6; the old code gives 6.3e-1 / 1.1 on the same grid (step2e_test_bounds.out). _gyro_difference also then built its time slot with _time_slot directly instead of _proj(concatenate([0, s])) — bit-identical value and gradient over 2880 pairs, both dtypes (step2e_time_slot.out), the same GPU fusion-shape reason as the _addition entry below.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• is_in_manifold/is_in_tangent_space now test the residual on the time slot instead of the Lorentz form. The old check compared ⟨x,x⟩_L against -1/c (or ⟨v,x⟩_L against 0), a residual that grows like 2·x₀ times the honest time-slot discrepancy and is itself obtained as a difference of two O(cosh²a) numbers. Comparing x₀ (or v₀) against √(1/c + ‖x_s‖²) directly removes both factors: an explicit atol now bounds |x₀ - √(1/c + ‖x_s‖²)|, where it previously bounded roughly 2·x₀ times that quantity.
  • lorentz_midpoint's normalizer is O(N·M·D) — one (…, N, M, D) broadcast difference, not a pairwise (…, M, M, D) Gram. The O(M²) key-Gram form never shipped in a release: on this branch it existed only between the accuracy fix and the variance-form rewrite that replaced it (see the ### Fixed entry above). Cost: see the next entry.

  • Historical cost of the preceding sweep at 5b756df against b586169 (as-is) — AOT-compiled executables, float32, batch 4096, c = 0.5, spatial radius ≈ 3, forward and nnx.value_and_grad forward+backward; CPU is XLA:CPU on the development box, GPU an A100 with XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0 (logs/2026-09-08_hyperboloid_tangent_primitives/cost_summary.md, probe_cost_{b586169,5b756df}.out, probe_cost_gpu_{b586169,5b756df}.out). The rows are workload functions, plus the explicitly named single optimizer step; they are not complete training-update, current-performance, or convergence measurements. They predate 757a910 and the origin-derivative repairs.

    workload CPU as-is ms CPU new ms CPU ratio GPU as-is ms GPU new ms GPU ratio PLFC gyro-bias fwd 6.2048 2.2965 0.370 0.2561 0.2510 0.980 PLFC gyro-bias fwd+bwd 13.8245 6.3049 0.456 0.6084 0.6258 1.03 GyroBatchNorm(train) fwd 9.0924 5.5412 0.609 0.5463 0.4806 0.880 GyroBatchNorm(train) fwd+bwd 13.4201 7.6611 0.571 0.7203 0.5613 0.779 HyperboloidGyroRMSNorm fwd+bwd 3.5352 3.5132 0.994 — — — HyperbolicFullAttention fwd 12.0482 89.9417 7.47 0.6080 0.9836 1.62 HyperbolicFullAttention fwd+bwd 31.1128 139.1628 4.47 1.4532 2.1561 1.48 LorentzResidual fwd 0.8921 2.0828 2.33 — — — LorentzResidual fwd+bwd 1.7535 3.0969 1.77 — — — Busemann head fwd 2.1609 98.2874 45.5 — — — Busemann head fwd+bwd 4.4315 131.7908 29.7 — — — _busemann_score K=256 fwd+bwd — — — 0.3418 0.8373 2.45 _busemann_score K=1000 fwd+bwd — — — 0.5406 2.3974 4.43 riemannian_adam one step 21.2513 21.7737 1.02 — — — Poincare.dist (vmap) 5.2551 2.1213 0.404 — — — Poincare.addition (vmap) 4.5814 5.3327 1.16 — — — Poincare.logmap (vmap) 8.5312 7.9924 0.937 — — — HypLinearPoincarePP fwd 3.4088 3.3689 0.988 — — — HypLinearPV fwd 1.3097 1.2538 0.957 — — — ProperVelocity.expmap (vmap) 5.8779 6.7439 1.15 — — — horo_projection (vmap, K=3) 5.8367 7.2006 1.23 — — — frechet_mean (max_iters=100) 73.4981 52.3895 0.713 — — — prim Hyperboloid.addition value_and_grad(both) 17.3033 3.4826 0.201 — — — prim Hyperboloid.expmap 2.8512 4.9346 1.73 — — — prim Hyperboloid.tangent_inner 1.9195 6.7360 3.51 — — — prim Hyperboloid.ptransp 9.7918 8.8648 0.905 — — — prim lorentz_midpoint 3.9228 111.3655 28.4 — — —

    Every consumer of the gyro-addition is about 2x faster on CPU and unchanged on GPU. GyroBatchNorm is 0.57–0.61x as-is on CPU; on the A100 it measured 0.78–0.88x in one run and 0.96–0.97x on the repeat, i.e. unchanged within GPU noise — so the key-Gram intermediate's 148x (CPU) / 14.5x (GPU) never reached a release (the numbers in the key-Gram column of the summary). The rows above 1.5x and why: attention and the lorentz_midpoint primitive on CPU because XLA:CPU materialises the variance form's (…, N, M, D) difference (Mflop only 1.3x for attention) while XLA:GPU fuses it (attention 1.62x / 1.48x on the A100), LorentzResidual on CPU for its pairwise polar frame, the Busemann head (CPU streaming of the exact broadcast-reduce; 2.1–4.4x on the A100 at 0.41–2.40 ms absolute, the decided trade), prim Hyperboloid.expmap and tangent_inner (three reductions instead of one; only the Riemannian optimizer's second moment and frechet_mean call them, and the optimizer step is 1.02x). GPU repeatability from the repeat run probe_cost_gpu_5b756df_rep2.out: worst 39.4% on the float64-island GEMM K=1000 fwd row, 24.1% on GyroBatchNorm fwd+bwd, so GPU ratios inside ±1.3x are noise. - The batched Busemann head, nn_layers.busemann_core._busemann_score, and the vmapped busemann shared by the Busemann MLR/FC layers use the same projected-coordinate formula as Hyperboloid.busemann. The measurements in probe_midpoint_horopca_busemann_pv_9093ea7.out describe the preceding large-radius value repair; the current formula additionally preserves the constrained origin derivative. - Hyperboloid._addition builds its time slot with _time_slot directly instead of _proj(concatenate([0, s])). Bit-identical value and gradient; a GPU-only performance fix. The dead zero-slot pad/slice pair in the backward made XLA:GPU root a multi-output fusion in a column reduction instead of a row reduction: on an A100 (jax 0.9.1, float32, c=0.5, B=4096, D=64) the dominant kernel of that fusion, input_multiply_reduce_fusion, cost 1769.5 µs/call as the boost was first merged (diag_plfc_kernels_900f054.out) — against 87.9 µs/call for the same fusion before the boost rewrite existed at all (diag_plfc_kernels_b586169.out, the pre-boost round-trip spelling) — and now costs 53.9 µs/call (diag_plfc_kernels_fixed.out). Total device time for HypLinearHyperboloidPLFC(65, 65, use_gyro_bias=True)'s forward+backward kernels drops from 2052.2 µs/call to 356.4 µs/call; the AOT wall-clock forward+backward (median of 50 calls) is 0.5810 ms fixed (diag_plfc_gpu_fixed.out), forward alone 0.1738 ms. Output and ∂L/∂gyro_bias are bit-identical to the round-trip spelling.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• ProperVelocity.gyro_difference(x, y, c) — the PV gyrovector difference (⊖x) ⊕ y, evaluated through the exact direct lift to Hyperboloid.gyro_difference. Use it for centering and for differences expected to lie much closer to the origin than their operands. ProperVelocityGyroBatchNorm uses it for centering.
  • HyperbolicFullAttention(score_dtype=...). An opt-in float64 island for the Lorentzian similarity score: the two einsums and the 2 + 2⟨Q,K⟩_L / scale / bias / causal-mask arithmetic run in score_dtype and are cast back to the working dtype before the softmax. score_dtype=None (the default) leaves the score path unchanged op for op. The GEMM-formed score has no cancellation-free spelling — any matrix product of the ambient coordinates returns the Gram matrix to absolute eps — so past a ≈ 8 (c=1, scale=1) the absolute score error eps·cosh(a_q)·cosh(a_k)/(c·scale) exceeds what softmax can resolve; score_dtype=jnp.float64 fixes the arithmetic but not float32 storage of the activations themselves — see docs/user-guide/numerical-stability.md.
  • Hyperboloid.gyro_difference(x, y, c) — (⊖x) ⊕ y for centering a batch on its mean and differences expected to lie closer to the origin than their operands. It is mathematically identical to addition(scalar_mul(-1, x), y), using a Cartesian inverse boost when either endpoint's scaled spatial radius is at most 1e-1 and the stable polar frame otherwise. The historical equivalence measurements in step2c_gyro_difference_equivalence.out predate the Cartesian origin repair. HyperboloidGyroBatchNorm uses this method for centering.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The origin Jacobian of Hyperboloid.expmap / expmap_0 was √c·I instead of I for every c < 1. It bit whenever the tangent vector satisfied ‖v‖ ≲ 1e-15/√c, the zero tangent included: the divisor of the sinh(t)/t ratio carried a second MIN_NORM floor (denom = floor_at(√c·‖v‖, MIN_NORM)) that the numerator did not, so at v = 0 the ratio evaluated to √c·1e-15 / 1e-15 = √c rather than 1 and the whole spatial Jacobian came out scaled by √c — a zero-initialised gyro-bias saw its first gradient scaled by 0.32 at c = 0.1, 0.55 at c = 0.3, in both dtypes (c ≥ 1 was unaffected, since the floor is inactive there). Found by an independent numerics review. The divisor is now the same floored t = √c·‖v‖, which is ≥ √c·1e-15 > 0 and normal in both dtypes, so sinh(t)/t is exactly 1 there; the Poincaré, stereographic and proper-velocity exponential maps already divided by a single floored quantity and are unchanged. test_hyperboloid_expmap_at_the_origin_has_the_identity_jacobian pins the identity at c ∈ {0.1, 0.3, 1, 2.5} in both dtypes, and test_hyperboloid_gyro_bias_at_the_origin_has_a_nonzero_jacobian now runs at c = 0.1 as well as c = 1.
  • The norm-rescale divisor was not an exact power of two in float64 on CUDA, so the rescale it exists to make rounding-free put a rounding into every division it scales. _pow2_divisor built the divisor with jnp.ldexp, which computes m · 2**e and lowers to an XLA power — a ~1 ulp transcendental on CUDA rather than an exact exponent shift. On an A100 (jax 0.9.1) that came out an ulp low for 75 of the 600 binades k ∈ [-300, 300); ldexp(1.0, -33) returns one ulp below 2**-33. The divisor is now built by masking the mantissa bits off m, which leaves 2**floor(log2 m) exactly on every backend, with the old minexp floor replaced by a finfo.tiny floor (a subnormal m masks to 0). Affected safe_norm, safe_hypot, safe_hypot_norm and safe_normalize on GPU, in float64 only — float32 was already exact on both backends, and CPU float64 was too; values there are bit-identical before and after (checked over every binade of both dtypes plus 0, inf, nan, the subnormals, finfo.tiny and finfo.max). It showed up as test_the_norm_rescale_adds_no_rounding_of_its_own failing on GPU with mean ulp distance 0.27–0.34 against 0.000 on CPU. test_the_rescale_divisor_is_an_exact_power_of_two_on_every_backend now pins zero mantissa bits and the correct binade over the full exponent range of both dtypes.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Float32 matmul precision is now split by what the dot product computes, not by where it lives, and there is no hyperbolix-specific knob for it. MATMUL_PRECISION = jax.lax.Precision.HIGHEST is pinned on the geometry and is not user-configurable: the vector-vector reductions in manifolds/ (behind dist, addition, gyration, expmap, logmap, ptransp, tangent_inner, egrad2rgrad, the Lorentz inner product, the Busemann coordinate and the boundary factors) and the HoroPCA contractions in decomposition/; lorentz_midpoint and the Poincaré poincare_weighted_midpoint, the two Fréchet-mean normalizers whose cancellation-free identity only holds to O(eps) on float32-accurate inputs; the conv_general_dilated_patches patch extraction in the hyperboloid, Poincaré and proper-velocity convolutions, which XLA implements as a convolution against a 0/1 filter — a pure data copy, where TF32 would round every input to a 10-bit mantissa for no throughput at all; the attention score and aggregation einsums in hyperboloid_attention.py (the Lorentzian similarity, the softmax scores and weighted values, the linear-attention kernel sums) and the spatial residual projection added to that aggregate; and the point-to-hyperplane einsums — HypRegressionHyperboloid and FGGLorentzMLR plus the three batched _compute_mlr einsums in manifolds/hyperboloid.py, poincare.py and proper_velocity.py — whose asinh argument is a difference of a radial and an angular term that cancels. That last pin reaches into the hidden layers too: HypLinearHyperboloidPLFC, HypLinearPoincarePP, HypLinearPV, HypConv2DHyperboloidILNN, HypConv2DPoincare and HypConv2DPV are those einsums applied to their own kernel, so their weight GEMM runs at HIGHEST as well. What the head's pin costs, measured on an H100 against 1.1.2 (every dot at TF32): the HypRegressionHyperboloid forward alone, B=1e7, 10 classes, is 2.6x at D=128 and 2.0x at D=32 (1.02x of 1.2.0, which pinned it too); in a training step expmap_0 → HTCLinear ×2 → HypRegressionHyperboloid at B=262144, D=128 the pin is the residual 1.05x over 1.1.2 once the GEMM pin and the norms are given back (the same step was 1.00x on the tree before the split). The hyperbolic attention layers, whose score and aggregation einsums are pinned, are 1.25–1.31x of 1.1.2 at (8, 256, 257) and 0.76–0.80x of 1.2.0. On an A100 (jax 0.9.1) the float32-vs-float64 relative error of lorentz_midpoint is 4.6e-5 … 2.6e-4 at the TF32 default against 2.6e-8 … 1.6e-7 under HIGHEST, a ~2000x difference; the eager float32 gradient of the hyperboloid MLR goes from 1.5e-4 to 2.7e-7 relative over the same switch.
  • The layer weight GEMMs carry no precision keyword at all and follow JAX's own jax_default_matmul_precision — TF32 on Ampere/Hopper. HTCLinear — the attention Q/K/V projections included — FGGLinear/FGGConv2D, the FHCNN and FHNN linear forwards, HypLinearPoincare, HypVQMLRPoincare's implicit-codebook matmul and hybrid_regularization's nnx.Linear. One of them carries a cancellation and is still left on the default: the FGG hidden dot x @ V absorbs the Minkowski metric into V, so the -x0*V0 + <x_s, V_s> cancellation happens inside one accumulation — the same product FGGLorentzMLR pins — and the comment on the jnp.matmul in nn_layers/hyperboloid_linear._fgg_linear_forward says so. It is left there deliberately: at depth 16, c = 1, input geodesic radius 5, an FGGLinear stack's float32 parameter-gradient error under the default is 0.199 % relative L2 against a float64 reference and its input-gradient error 0.274 %, against 1.539 % / 2.013 % for an HTCLinear stack, which has no cancellation at all — so the in-accumulation cancellation is not what dominates there (independent A100 measurement, jax 0.9.1, logs/2026-09-06_numerics_independent_review/training/gpu/depth.json; under global HIGHEST the same four cells are 8.0e-7 / 1.0e-6 and 2.5e-6 / 1.2e-5). Those depth-16 numbers are the worst cell of a 24-cell grid (depths 2/8/16, c ∈ {0.1, 1}, input radius {0.5, 5}), one initialisation and one input draw per cell and no seeds — grid maxima at n = 1, not means, and the HTC stack's measured radius climb (≈0.35 nats per layer at large radius) and the hypothesis linking it to the depth-16 error are in the hyperbolix/utils/precision.py docstring. At depth 2 the choice is invisible in training: 5 seeds per arm, D = 128, B = 256, c = 1, 2 000 Adam updates, mean heldout loss 0.27736 (default) against 0.27738 (HIGHEST) for HTC and 0.28610 against 0.28614 for FGG, on a seed spread of ~0.015–0.017. HTCLinear is where that choice is visible in the test suite: test_attn_output_shape_and_jit and test_causal_first_token_self_only compare two lowerings of the same algebra at a 1e-5 tolerance, which TF32's run-to-run rounding exceeds, so both now wrap their forward passes in jax.default_matmul_precision("highest") — the tolerances are unchanged and the TF32 values are not wrong. These are the sites where HIGHEST actually costs throughput — it replaces one TF32 pass with a three-pass float32 emulation, measured +5.5 % on a jitted hyperbolic attention forward — so the trade is the user's to make, through JAX rather than through a hyperbolix-specific attribute: jax.config.update("jax_default_matmul_precision", "highest"), or scoped, with jax.default_matmul_precision("highest"):. Both are jit-cache aware (changing them re-traces), and both cover the pinned sites too, so one line runs the whole package in full float32. A deep, fully hyperbolic stack is a good reason to set it: a TF32 error introduced in an early layer's weight GEMM is carried by every layer after it, and it is not small. Measured on an A100 (jax 0.9.1, ambient dim 33, batch 64, c in {0.1, 1.0} x spatial radius in {0.5, 5, 20}, float32 against a float64 reference): FGGLinear 2.6e-4 at the TF32 default against 6.8e-8 under HIGHEST, FGGLorentzMLR 1.3e-4 … 3.6e-4 against 3.6e-8 … 9.6e-8 — roughly ~1e-4 against ~1e-7 on the layers, three of float32's seven significant digits. HIGHEST is a no-op on CPU (no TF32 path) and for float64 anywhere.
  • The per-sample norms that 1.2.0 measurably made slower are a single reduction again — and only those. A site is converted where 1.2.0 measured slower (hyperboloid expmap_0 1.28x, HTCLinear forward+backward 1.12x, on both A100 and H100) or where PR #75 raised the compiled kernel / reduction count. That is: Hyperboloid.proj/proj_batch/dist_0 (both version slots); the shared gyrovector proj/proj_batch behind Poincare and Stereographic, and Poincare.expmap; and spatial_to_hyperboloid (so HTCLinear), the FHCNN linear forward and the FGG linear forward. Everywhere else 1.2.0's max-scaled two-pass norm stays, with its full-range guarantee. In isolation that costs something — about 1.2–1.35x the one-pass form on a forward pass in float32 (h_logmap_0 and Poincare.expmap_0 at D = 32/B = 4096 and D = 128/B = 262144, c ∈ {0.1, 1}: 1.202–1.343, independent A100 measurement, jax 0.9.1, logs/2026-09-06_numerics_independent_review/timing/norm/ — this range rests on that measurement alone; the 1.28x above is a v1.2.0-vs-v1.1.2 tree ratio of a converted site, not a one-pass/two-pass swap of a retained one) — but inside a training step it shrinks to ≤ ~1.05x (0.92–1.05x on the same probe's complete-step and HTC-chart rows), which is why the two-pass norm is kept wherever the operand's magnitude is unbounded. The retained sites: hyperboloid logmap_0 (which measured faster in 1.2.0), the pairwise dist/logmap polar frame, hyperboloid and Poincaré tangent_norm, Poincare.expmap_0 (no measured change either way), the FHNN linear forward, the linear-attention focus_transform (converting it measured no speedup of its own), every ProperVelocity operation and the proper-velocity isometry maps, the Poincaré metric-tensor distances, the rest of Stereographic, Euclidean and ProductManifold, and the wrapped-normal log_prob. The converted spellings are safe_sqrt(sum(v**2)) where the input can be exactly zero, a plain sqrt(const + sum(v**2)) where a strictly positive constant is added, and floor_at(..., MIN_NORM) around either where the norm is a divisor. Every gradient fix from 1.2.0 is kept: safe_sqrt's double-where gives the same exact 0 and exactly-zero VJP at the zero vector that safe_norm did, so jax.grad at coincident points and at the origin stays finite.
  • Past float32 coordinate 1.8e19 the converted sites give up their answer, and what they give instead was measured rather than argued. That coordinate is geodesic radius ~45 at c = 1 and ~139 at c = 0.1, in float32; a network out there is already diverging, and inf is the intended signal rather than a plausible finite answer. Measured, float32, c = 1: Hyperboloid.proj/proj_batch give x0 = inf with the spatial part unchanged and no NaN; dist_0 gives inf on both version slots; spatial_to_hyperboloid/HTCLinear and the FHCNN forward give x0 = inf with no NaN; the FGG linear forward gives a non-finite output (NaN or inf, depending on the input — an all-NaN output on the probe's 5e19 spatial input, inf with no NaN on a second, crafted one); the Poincaré and κ-stereographic boundary clamps give the origin — a finite point, with a finite (exactly zero) gradient there — because x * (max_norm / inf) is the zero vector, the pre-1.2.0 behaviour; and Poincare.expmap gives the base point, a finite point, inheriting the same clamp. Two of the converted sites therefore do saturate to a finite point, and that is the clamp's documented behaviour. Everything on the two-pass norm — Poincare.expmap_0, which still returns the correct boundary point, and the linear-attention focus_transform included — behaves exactly as in 1.2.0.
  • The maximum radius the converted origin-chart operations can represent drops with it. For proj and dist_0 the ceiling used to be x₀'s — the two-pass norm never formed ‖x_s‖², so what bound the radius was cosh(a)/√c ≤ finfo.max, i.e. a = ln(2·finfo.max): radius ~89 in float32 / ~710 in float64 at c = 1 (89.416 / 710.476, the same number as arcsinh(finfo.max), since sinh(a) and cosh(a) leave the dtype together). It is now the coordinate limit sinh(a)/√c < sqrt(finfo.max) — radius ~45 in float32 and ~356 in float64. logmap_0 and the pairwise dist/logmap keep the two-pass norm and so keep a ceiling of that order: logmap_0 reads only ‖y_s‖ and keeps the old ~89 / ~710 exactly, while the pairwise pair binds a fraction of a radius earlier at e^a/√c ≤ finfo.max (a = ln(finfo.max), 88.72 / 709.78), because _polar_frame forms u = x₀ + ‖x_s‖ and returns ±inf once that overflows. Every hyperbolic model in the literature lives four to five orders of magnitude inside every one of these limits.
  • safe_norm, safe_hypot_norm and safe_normalize remain public and are what every unconverted per-sample site and every once-per-forward weight norm still use. safe_hypot is a hot-path two-leg scalar composer, not a weight-norm primitive: the hyperboloid polar frame builds its radial and angular legs with it.
  • One deliberate value change: the hyperboloid time slot is now sqrt(1/c + sum(x_s**2)) instead of sqrt((1/sqrt(c))**2 + sum(x_s**2)), one rounding fewer and in the more accurate direction (Hyperboloid.proj/proj_batch, nn_layers.hyperboloid_core.spatial_to_hyperboloid, and the FHCNN/FGG layer forwards; isometry_mappings.pv_to_hyperboloid keeps 1.2.0's spelling). Everywhere else safe_norm/safe_hypot_norm were bit-identical to sqrt(sum)/sqrt(sum + q**2) on the finite domain, so values move only by XLA association noise (0-2 ulp).
  • The hyperboloid time slot carries a custom_jvp whose only job is the backward's XLA fusion shape. With the one-reduction sqrt(1/c + sum(x_s**2)), XLA:GPU fused the backward's reduction into a full-width Triton kernel and left the cotangent's re-embedding pad as a standalone copy of the whole batch, so jax.grad of proj/expmap_0 at B=1e7, D=128 ran 1.35x/1.76x slower than 1.1.2 on an H100 even though the forward was as fast; v1.1.2 avoided this only through the maximum(…, MIN_NORM) its VJP happened to place between the reduce and the sqrt. The module-private _time_slot rule states the same derivative AD derives (the 1/c cotangent 1/(2·x0) included, so a traced LearnableCurvature is unaffected) and puts a lax.optimization_barrier on the per-row 1/x0, which restores 1.1.2's kernel structure (proj.grad 3/1, expmap_0.grad 7/3 kernels/reductions at D=128). Forward values are bit-identical; jax.jvp/jacfwd keep working. test_hyperboloid_time_slot_custom_jvp_matches_plain_autodiff checks value, gradient, forward-mode tangent and the curvature cotangent against the rule-free spelling. The fusion effect it fixes is shape- and consumer-dependent, so it will not reproduce everywhere: it appeared in float32 on jax 0.9.1 at B ≥ 1e6, at both D = 32 and D = 128 (expmap_0.grad 1.48x of 1.1.2 at B = 1e6 and 1.76x at B = 1e7 for D = 128, and 1.60x at B = 1e7 for D = 32, with proj.grad 1.35x at either width; absent at B = 1e5, 0.98x at D = 128 — logs/2026-09-04_safe_norm_hot_path_revert/RESULTS_31403c2.md, .../vda/timing_D{32,128}/ and .../vda3/timing_D{32,128}/, two different H100 hosts with every ratio against a v1.1.2 arm from the same host and run), and only for a backward that materialises the full (B, n) cotangent, e.g. jax.grad of a sum over the output. With a scalar-loss consumer the pad fuses anyway: an independent A100 measurement of jax.grad(mean(f(x)**2)) at B ≤ 262144, D = 128 put the barrier arm within ~1 % of the rule-free spelling for expmap_0 forward+backward at the large shape (1.003-1.006 at both c = 1 and c = 0.1, against either spelling without the barrier); the proj rows of the same run are noisier (one contaminated round).
  • One extreme-radius test row moved from float32 to float64. It was exercising the retired overflow guard rather than the algorithm, so it follows the guard rather than being loosened; tolerances are unchanged. In tests/test_manifold_oracles.py, test_hyperboloid_dist_and_logmap_to_the_origin_match_the_origin_variants now takes a per-dtype radius grid — float32 stops at 43, float64 keeps 45. What binds is the spatial coordinate sinh(a)/sqrt(c), which passes float32's 1.845e19 at radius 45 for c = 0.3, where the converted dist_0 returns inf by policy; exactly that one cell of the grid crosses the threshold, and 43 is the repo's existing float32 radial ceiling. This narrows the float32 coverage rather than preserving it: the radius-45 cell is no longer exercised in float32 at all, only in float64. The pairwise oracle rows are untouched, because the pairwise dist/logmap keep the two-pass norm.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• The smooth_clamp on the asinh argument of every MLR head is gone, and with it the clamping_factor and smoothing_factor parameters of Hyperboloid.compute_mlr, Poincare.compute_mlr_pp, ProperVelocity.compute_mlr and the four _compute_mlr helpers, plus every layer that only carried them to forward: HypRegressionHyperboloid, HypRegressionPoincare, HypRegressionPoincarePP, HypRegressionPV, HypLinearHyperboloidPLFC, HypLinearPoincarePP, HypLinearPV, HypConv2DHyperboloidILNN, HypConv2DPoincare, HypConv2DPV and HypVQMLRPoincare. This is a signature break: drop the two keywords at the call site. asinh is defined on all of R with derivative 1/√(1+x²) ≤ 1, so it needs no guard — the only infinite argument comes from a point that has already overflowed the float32 manifold, and the clamp turned that into a finite, plausible logit and hid the divergence; the logit is now inf and the loss NaN, which is the failure you want to see. The bound was also dtype-dependent (log(2/eps): ±16.6355 in float32 against ±36.7368 in float64), so the two dtypes disagreed by design: measured with HypRegressionHyperboloid at c = 1, geodesic radius 5, default init, batch 256 × 10 classes, the float32 logits sat 9.4e-2 (D = 128, 1.2% of cells clamped) and 1.8e-1 (D = 32, 22.4% clamped) from the float64 ones relative to the largest logit, identical under TF32 and HIGHEST; with the clamp gone the same cells agree to 6.4e-7 / 4.6e-7. Every clamped cell also had an exactly zero input gradient (smooth_clamp's slope past its bound is exp(-50·d)), freezing those points under SGD, and at c = 1 with the shipped init the float32 bound first bit at geodesic radius 4.25 (D = 32) / 4.75 (D = 128) — well inside the range the library documents as float32-reliable. Neither reference clamps this quantity: HNN++ (mil-tokyo/hyperbolic_nn_plusplus) guards only the 1 - c‖x‖² denominator and the weight norms at a flat 1e-15, and HCNN's LorentzMLR (kschwethelm/HyperbolicCV) has no guard at all; the line came from the author's earlier PyTorch code (univie-dm/hyperbolic_math, helpers.py, "Improve the performance by smoothly clamping the input of asinh()") with no recorded rationale. smooth_clamp itself stays in hyperbolix.utils.math_utils and is unchanged
  • The three float32 overflow oracles in tests/test_manifold_oracles.py are retired, since the guard they tested is gone. test_hyperboloid_proj_time_slot_survives_the_float32_overflow becomes test_hyperboloid_proj_time_slot_is_exact_at_an_enormous_radius in float64, and test_poincare_proj_clamps_a_far_point_to_the_boundary_not_to_the_origin moves to float64; both then assert the algorithm rather than the dtype's range. test_hyperboloid_expmap_0_saturates_to_a_consistent_point_not_an_infinite_time_slot cannot move — sinh clips its argument at 0.99*log(finfo.max) in both dtypes, so the capped spatial value squared overflows in float64 too — and is replaced by test_hyperboloid_expmap_0_past_the_sinh_cap_is_infinite_not_nan, which pins the weaker but real contract: x0 = inf, spatial part finite, no NaN.
  • Hyperboloid.dist/dist_0 slots 2 and 3 (VERSION_LEGACY, VERSION_LEGACY_SMOOTHENED) are gone; a version_idx outside {0, 1} now raises ValueError. The explicit check is needed because lax.switch silently clamps an out-of-range index into range, so a stale version_idx=2 would have quietly run the smoothened arm instead of failing. The two slots were added in 1.1.2 / 1.2.0 by the very fixes that made them obsolete (the cancellation-free dist rewrite and the origin-chart dist_0 rewrite); at 1.1.1 the switch had only two slots, so no pre-fix code ever passed 2 or 3, and pre-fix numbers remain reproducible by installing hyperbolix==1.1.1 from PyPI. For the record, the four golden values the deleted regression test pinned — on-sheet point at spatial radius 1e-3, c = 1, dim 8, direction e1, true geodesic radius 9.99999833e-4 — were: slot 2 float32 0.0015440807910636067, slot 2 float64 0.0009999998333921221, slot 3 float64 0.16632065504083338, slot 3 float32 0.16632071137428284 (CPU; ±1 ulp on an A100)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Every zero-initialised hyperboloid gyro-bias was frozen at its init value: ∂(x ⊕ b)/∂b at b = origin was exactly the zero matrix, in both dtypes. dist_0 short-circuited on a bitwise at_origin guard (jnp.where(at_origin, 0.0, res)); logmap_0 scales the spatial part by dist_0(y)/‖y_s‖ and inherited it; Lorentz gyro addition x ⊕ y = Exp_x(PT_{0→x}(Log_0(y))) inherited it in turn. A bias parameter that starts at the origin, which is what use_gyro_bias=True does, therefore received an exactly-zero gradient at step 0 and never left. Affected layers: HypLinearHyperboloidPLFC, HypConv2DHyperboloidILNN, HypLinearHyperboloidBusemann. Measured gyro-bias gradient L2 at init (c = 1, dim 8, batch 4, dist_0 loss, before → after): float32 0.0 → 1.37 (PLFC), 0.0 → 4.24 (ILNN conv), 0.0 → 3.07 (Busemann FC); float64 0.0 → 1.48, 0.0 → 5.37, 0.0 → 1.83. In float32 the gradient was additionally ~1400x over-scaled the moment the bias left the origin, because the acosh floor below was divided by the true radius: the PLFC gradient at bias radius 1e-6 was 1535x its value at 1e-2, a ratio that is now 1.06x. The Poincaré HypLinearPoincareBusemann gyro-bias goes through Möbius addition and was never affected (7.64 before and after). A model trained with a gyro-bias on any of the three hyperboloid layers was trained with that bias pinned to the origin; retraining under this fix changes results.

  • Hyperboloid dist_0/logmap_0 recovered the geodesic radius from the time coordinate x₀, which cannot resolve a small radius; they now read it off the spatial part. dist_0 was acosh(clip(√c·x₀, 1))/√c. On the sheet x₀ = cosh(√c·d)/√c ≈ (1 + c·d²/2)/√c, so d survives only to sqrt(eps) resolution (relative error eps/(2·c·d²)), and acosh's 1 + 10·eps domain clamp flattened every float32 radius below sqrt(20·eps)/√c = 1.5441e-3 onto that floor value (1.5441e-3 was returned for every such point, 1500x too large at radius 1e-6; only the bitwise origin returned 0). The smoothened arm was worse: smooth_clamp_min (β = 50) adds ln2/50 to the acosh argument, i.e. a floor of acosh(1 + ln2/50)/√c = 0.16632/√c under every point that is not bitwise the origin, in both dtypes (measured: it returned 0.16632 at every radius ≤ 1e-2 and 0.1815 at radius 0.1, agreeing with the true value only from radius ≈ 1). Slot 0 is now the exact on-sheet identity arcsinh(√c·‖x_s‖)/√c, with no domain clamp and a derivative bounded by 1; slot 1 is the same with the spatial radius floored in quadrature at 20·eps, a floor of arcsinh(20·eps)/√c (2.4e-6/√c float32, 4.4e-15/√c float64) that equals the pairwise smoothened floor 2·arcsinh(10·eps)/√c from 1.1.2 to first order. logmap_0 is now [0, arcsinh(u)/u · y_s] with u = √c‖y_s‖: it no longer routes through dist_0's version switch, ‖log_0(y)‖ = dist_0(y) holds by construction instead of by cancelling a floored numerator against an unfloored denominator, and the trailing tangent_proj is dropped (it is the identity at the origin, but it routes through the Minkowski inner product, which turns one inf spatial coordinate into an all-NaN vector). scalar_mul is now literally exp_0(r · log_0(x)); its old normalize-then-rescale detour carried a sqrt(max(‖v‖², MIN_NORM)) floor, an effective 3.16e-8 floor on ‖log_0 x‖ that was invisible only while the larger acosh floor sat in front of it. Median relative error at c = 1, dim 8 (A100, jax 0.9.1; the CPU backend and jax 0.11.0 agree in every floored cell):

    radius float32 dist_0 float32 log_0(exp_0(v)) float64 dist_0 float64 round trip 1e-6 1.5e3 → 2.5e-9 1.5e3 → 0 4.4e-5 → 0 4.4e-5 → 1.3e-16 1e-3 5.4e-1 → 9.8e-8 5.4e-1 → 0 5.9e-11 → 0 1.5e-10 → 1.2e-16 1e-2 5.0e-4 → 2.7e-8 5.2e-4 → 0 1.0e-12 → 1.7e-16 8.3e-13 → 1.2e-16 0.1 3.5e-6 → 1.8e-8 1.4e-7 → 3.9e-8 7.6e-15 → 1.4e-16 9.5e-15 → 1.1e-16 1 to 40 ≤7.1e-8 → ≤5.2e-8 ≤1.0e-7 → ≤8.8e-8 ≤1.3e-16 → ≤1.9e-16 ≤1.4e-16 → ≤1.4e-16

    Consumers that inherit the fix with no change of their own: gyro addition, scalar_mul, logmap's origin fallback, HyperboloidGyroRMSNorm (it divides by dist_0, so in float32 every sample inside radius 1.5e-3 was mis-normalised), and the three gyro-bias layers above. Pairwise dist(origin, x) is a separate code path and still carries an O(eps/r) relative error from the _polar_frame gap term near the origin (float32: 4.6e-2 at radius 1e-6, ~1e-3 at 1e-4); closing that is a planned separate change, so prefer dist_0 for distances to the origin. Supersedes the claim in the 1.1.2 entry below that origin-chart operations "read the radius straight off the ambient time coordinate and were never affected": reading it off the time coordinate is precisely the defect fixed here. That entry's two-point cancellation claims, and expmap_0, are unchanged

  • On an Ampere or Hopper GPU, lorentz_midpoint and the three hyperbolic attention layers silently ran their matmuls in TF32, costing ~2000x accuracy in the one place the library cannot afford it. XLA:GPU defaults float32 matmuls to TF32, whose 10-bit mantissa carries ~1e-3 relative error against float32's ~1e-7. lorentz_midpoint's whole design is a cancellation-free identity in which every rounded term is O(‖delta‖²), so that the normalizer stays accurate at any radius — TF32 is far coarser than the effect that identity exists to remove. Measured float32-vs-float64 relative error of lorentz_midpoint (A100, jax 0.9.1, c ∈ {0.1, 1.0} × ‖s‖ ∈ {0.5, 5, 20}): GPU default 4.6e-5 … 2.6e-4, GPU with the fix 2.6e-8 … 1.6e-7, CPU 2.6e-8 … 1.2e-7 — i.e. three of the seven significant digits were gone, with no warning, in every hyperbolic attention or Fréchet-mean computation on such a card. The worst site is HyperbolicFullAttention's Lorentzian similarity, which evaluates ⟨Q,K⟩_L = -Q₀K₀ + ⟨Q_s,K_s⟩ as the difference of two matmuls — the exact cancellation _polar_frame was written to avoid, with both halves produced by TF32 GEMMs, so the subtraction amplifies a ~1e-3 input error rather than a ~1e-7 one. Fixed by annotating the cancellation-sensitive dots with precision=jax.lax.Precision.HIGHEST through one documented constant, hyperbolix.nn_layers.hyperboloid_core.MATMUL_PRECISION: the three jnp.einsums in lorentz_midpoint, the ten score / Lorentz-inner-product / aggregate einsums in hyperboloid_attention.py, the spatial residual projection the linear and softmax variants add to that aggregate, and HTCLinear's matmul — the last because it produces the Q/K/V the Lorentz inner product then cancels, and a TF32 input makes an accurate cancellation pointless (annotating only the attention einsums left 6 of the 7 attention tests red; adding HTCLinear left 2; adding the residual projection cleared them). This turned 14 of the 21 GPU-only test failures green (all 7 attention, all 7 lorentz_midpoint). HIGHEST is a no-op on CPU (no TF32 path) and for float64 anywhere; the CPU outputs of lorentz_midpoint and of a HyperbolicFullAttention forward are bit-identical before and after, eager and jitted, in both dtypes. On a tensor-core GPU it does trade GEMM throughput for accuracy, since HIGHEST replaces one TF32 pass with a three-pass float32 emulation: a jitted HyperbolicFullAttention forward at B = 8, N = 256, 4 heads, head dim 64, float32 measured a median 1.84 ms with the fix vs 1.74 ms at the TF32 default, +5.5 % (A100-PCIE-40GB, 5 warmup + 20 timed calls; the card was idle but shared, so treat the ratio as indicative)

  • The hyperboloid MLR forward dot ran in TF32 on the same cards, for the same reason: _compute_mlr forms alpha = -x₀·sinh(√c·r)·‖z‖ + cosh(√c·r)·⟨x_s, z⟩, a difference whose second term is a matmul. The einsum now carries precision=HIGHEST (spelled out locally — manifolds/ must not import from nn_layers/). Measured on an A100 against a float64 reference at identical inputs: the eager float32 gradient of _compute_mlr improves from 1.5e-4 to 2.7e-7 relative; the forward was already accurate (1.1e-7) on both settings. This does not fix the separate, intermittent 1 % error in the jitted float32 gradient of the same function, which survives every precision setting; that one is the jnp.maximum tie-break in the next entry
  • The remaining float32 dots on manifold data still ran in TF32 on Ampere/Hopper — the x @ V matmuls where the Minkowski metric is absorbed into the weight matrix, and the HoroPCA and Poincaré-MLR contractions. PR #70 closed the Lorentz cancellations that are written as an explicit difference of two dots (lorentz_midpoint, the attention scores, the hyperboloid MLR); this closes the rest. FGGLinear, FGGLorentzMLR and HypRegressionHyperboloid evaluate ⟨x, V⟩_L as one x @ V with the metric folded into V, so the -x₀V₀ + ⟨x_s, V_s⟩ cancellation happens inside a single TF32 accumulation and the ~1e-3 input rounding lands directly on the cancelled result. Measured float32-vs-float64 relative error on an A100 (jax 0.9.1, ambient dim 33, batch 64, c ∈ {0.1, 1.0} × spatial radius ∈ {0.5, 5, 20}; median over the batch, before → after): FGGLinear 2.6e-4 → 6.8e-8 (a 3700-3900x improvement at every cell), FGGLorentzMLR 1.3e-4 … 3.6e-4 → 3.6e-8 … 9.6e-8 (2200-3800x), horo_projection 4.0e-4 … 4.9e-3 → 2.8e-7 … 2.4e-6 (1400-2600x, the ideal-span Minkowski projections), HoroPCA.transform 1.9e-4 … 2.3e-3 → 3.4e-7 … 4.3e-6 (520-1560x, the Fréchet-mean Lorentz boost x @ Bᵀ plus the component-frame read-off), and the Poincaré HNN++ MLR compute_mlr_pp 3.8e-5 … 1.4e-4 → 6.0e-8 … 2.2e-7 (440-1740x). The fix is one library-wide setting rather than a per-call keyword: MATMUL_PRECISION = jax.lax.Precision.HIGHEST now lives in hyperbolix.utils.precision — a neutral home both manifolds/ and nn_layers/ can import from, so manifolds/hyperboloid.py::_compute_mlr imports it instead of spelling lax.Precision.HIGHEST locally — and is attached to all 87 float32 dot products in the package that touch points, tangent vectors or hyperplane normals (70 of them newly). hyperbolix.nn_layers.hyperboloid_core.MATMUL_PRECISION re-exports it, so existing imports keep working unchanged. Covered: the Poincaré/κ-stereographic/proper-velocity/gyrovector-core jnp.dot reductions behind dist, addition, gyration, expmap, logmap, ptransp, tangent_inner, egrad2rgrad and the boundary factors 1 - c‖x‖²; the hyperboloid _minkowski_inner, _proj time reconstruction, polar-frame Gram-Schmidt, tangent_norm radial split and Busemann coordinate; the isometry maps between the three models; HypLinearHyperboloidFHCNN/FHNN and HypLinearPoincare's tangent-space matmuls; the Poincaré batch-norm weighted gyromidpoint; HypVQMLRPoincare's implicit-codebook matmul; and the hyperboloid/Poincaré/PV conv patch extraction (conv_general_dilated_patches carries ambient channels, time slot included). HIGHEST is a no-op on CPU and for float64 anywhere, and the change is verified bit-identical: 280 CPU arrays covering every touched public entry point, forward and jax.grad, eager and jitted, in both dtypes, match the base commit exactly. The single-vector jnp.dot sites measured no GPU change either way (XLA lowers a vector-vector dot to a reduction rather than a tensor-core GEMM), so those annotations are insurance against a future lowering or a batched rewrite rather than a behaviour change today
  • The ‖z‖ floor in the hyperboloid MLR silently zeroed the entire ∂‖z‖ branch of its gradient on GPU, for one output channel at a time, in roughly two of every three process launches. _compute_mlr floored the hyperplane-normal norm with jnp.linalg.norm(z, ...).clip(min=min_enorm), i.e. jnp.maximum(n, eps). That op's JVP is jax's tie-breaking _balanced_eq, g · [n == ans] / (1 + [eps == ans]) — it tests the operand n for bit equality with the result ans, which is sound only while the two are literally the same value in the compiled graph. XLA:GPU emits n = sqrt(sum(z*z)) twice in the compiled backward — once as its own small fusion, once recomputed inside the fusion that evaluates the ∂‖z‖ branch — and its per-process fusion autotuner picks the emitter for the first one by measured runtime, NATIVE_EMITTER or BLOCK_LEVEL_EMITTER (Triton). The two emitters disagree in the last bit of n for some rows; when they do, [n == ans] is false for that row, the derivative factor becomes 0, and the gradient returned for that output channel is exactly the one you would get by treating ‖z‖ as a constant. Measured on an A100 (jax 0.9.1, linear_plfc layer-contract inputs, float32 vs a float64 reference): jitted gradient relative error 1.0e-2 → 1.5e-7, and in a failing launch the affected row matched the ‖z‖-frozen gradient to 2.5e-8 while every other row was correct to 1.5e-7 — the branch was dropped, not perturbed. The reduced repro failed in 5 of 8 launches before and passed 7 of 7 after; test_gradient_contract[linear_plfc-f32] failed in 3 of 4 pytest launches before and passed 3 of 3 after. This was not conditioning: perturbing ‖z‖ by one float32 ulp in float64 — coherently, or independently at each of its three occurrences in the formula — moves the true gradient by at most 2.4e-7, five orders of magnitude short of the observed error. The floor is now jnp.where(n > min_enorm, n, min_enorm), which compares n against the constant (0.027 vs 1e-15 at these inputs) instead of against a differently-rounded copy of itself, so no 1-ulp disagreement can flip it. Forward values and the CPU gradient are bit-identical before and after in both dtypes, eager and jitted; only a NaN z behaves differently (maximum propagates the NaN, where floors it), which is already outside the function's contract. Flooring the squared sum instead (sqrt(maximum(Σz², eps²))) does not help — it keeps the same maximum tie-break and still failed 4 of 6 launches. The three XLA flags that hid the symptom (--xla_gpu_enable_cublaslt=false, --xla_gpu_autotune_level=0, --xla_gpu_enable_triton_gemm=false) each did so only by removing the emitter choice, not by fixing anything. The same hazard applies to every jnp.maximum(f(x), floor) on a differentiated path — the library has ~30 such MIN_NORM floors — but only this one has been observed to fire; a pure-JAX repro and a draft upstream report are in logs/2026-09-03_plfc_jit_grad/upstream/
  • The same GPU gradient-zeroing hazard is now closed at every other constant floor and clamp in the library — 76 sites. The mechanism is the one in the entry above: jnp.maximum(f(x), CONST)'s JVP is jax's _balanced_eq, which tests the operand for bit equality with the result, and XLA:GPU may compute the operand twice with emitters chosen per process by its fusion autotuner. When the two copies disagree by 1 ulp the whole gradient branch through the operand is silently zeroed. Only the MLR site had been observed to fire, but every constant floor on a differentiated path is exposed, so all of them are rewritten as a comparison against the constant, through three new one-line helpers in hyperbolix.utils.math_utils: floor_at(x, lo) = where(x < lo, lo, x), cap_at(x, hi) = where(x > hi, hi, x), and clamp_to(x, lo, hi) = cap_at(floor_at(x, lo), hi). The comparison direction is chosen so a NaN operand still propagates exactly as maximum/minimum/clip propagated it (NaN < lo is false, so the NaN is selected), which makes the forward value identical for every input — finite, NaN, and ±inf — at all 76 sites, in both dtypes, eager and jitted. Converted: the whole of manifolds/ (hyperboloid 23, poincaré 6, gyrovector core 8, stereographic 4, proper velocity 2, product 1, isometry mappings 3), distributions/ (2), decomposition/ (9), utils/ (8), and nn_layers/ (10).   • ProperVelocity._beta collapsed to 0 for any point past ‖x‖ = 1.8e19/√c. 1/sqrt(1 + c·dot(x, x)) overflows the same way, and _beta is the coefficient every PV gyro-operation is built from — _addition, _expmap, _logmap, _dpi_x, _tangent_inner — so one overflowing coordinate silently zeroed all of them. ‖x‖ = 1.8e19 is geodesic radius arcsinh(1.8e19) ≈ 45, well inside the range PV exists to serve: it is the unconstrained model, chosen precisely because it stays stable where the ball saturates. _beta_inv is now safe_hypot(1, √c·safe_norm(x)) and _beta its reciprocal; isometry_mappings.pv_to_poincare had the same expression and the same fix (there the overflow mapped a far-out PV point to the ball origin)
  • The FHNN linear/conv forward returned an all-inf spatial row for any float32 time coordinate past y0 = 1.844e19. _fhnn_forward recovered the target spatial norm from the hyperboloid constraint as sqrt(y0**2 - 1/c), and y0**2 overflows float32 at sqrt(FLT_MAX) = 1.844e19 — a regime capped_exp deliberately allows y0 to reach, since it caps a runaway scale at exp(0.99·log(FLT_MAX)) ≈ 6.1e37 precisely so the value stays finite. Measured on the parent (logs/2026-09-04_flags_batch/probe_diff_of_squares.py, c = 1): y0 = 1e20 gives [1.0e20, inf, -inf, inf] and d‖y_s‖/dy0 = 0 instead of 1. It is now the factored difference of squares sqrt(y0 - 1/√c) · sqrt(y0 + 1/√c), whose two factors are each strictly positive because y0 > 1/√c + eps holds by construction (additive floor, not a max): finite through y0 = 3e38, with ‖y_s‖/y0 → 1 to 1e-6 relative and finite gradients. This is the difference-of-squares counterpart of the safe_hypot sum-of-squares conversion above, and it was the one remaining site of its kind in the library. Values are not bit-identical in float32. Over a margin-stratified grid (y0 - 1/√c from 1e-2 to 1e19, c in {0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5}, logs/2026-09-04_flags_batch/probe_ordinary_range.py) the two forms differ by at most 3.1e-6 relative, at the smallest margins; above margin 1 it is 1-2 ulps.
